In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heat sensitivity of cells depends not only on the temperature of heating, the cell line used, and cell density but also on the cell culture conditions.
the thermosensitivity is not only determined by cell type but is also dependent on the cell cycle, cell density, and cell culture conditions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat sensitivity of cells is a complex phenomenon, and the results obtained by different investigators may not be directly comparable.
the thermosensitivity in terms of survival, morphological changes, and the thermally induced changes in protein synthesis are not necessarily correlated.
the heat sensitivity of the cell lines is determined by a combination of the thermosensitivity and the rate of cell proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermosensitivity in vitro of hepatoma cell lines may not be predictive of the thermosensitivity observed in vivo.
the thermosensitivity in vitro of rat hepatoma cell strains is not an intrinsic property of the cells but rather a function of the experimental conditions.
the use of a single cell type to study the heat sensitivity of cells may lead to erroneous conclusions.
